title: Mariner Pharma post-optimize savings workup
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet summarizes a customer-specific before/after savings analysis for Mariner Pharma after applying Redwood Optimize recommendations. Draft intended for SE review and customer readout. Focus: inference routes used by Mariner (clinical-assistant, ingestion-embeddings, reranker) and high-impact levers we expect to apply over a 3-month runway.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
Mariner currently spends ~ $46,800/month on inference for production traffic (baseline). Applying Redwood Optimize recommendations (mixed quantization, prefix caching, model routing for low-cost fallbacks, and request-level batching) we estimate a conservative savings of 36% (~$16,800/month) and an aggressive scenario up to 52% (~$24,400/month) if traffic characteristics remain stable and we adopt int8 quantization everywhere possible plus embedding batching improvements. Key tradeoffs: nominal increase in per-request latency for some routes (median +12–35ms) and an elevated QA review bucket during rollout (expected <1% of queries).

Baseline inputs (as instrumented by Mariner telemetry and our onboarding profiler):
- Monthly active tokens (generation + completion): 3,600,000,000 tokens/month
- Embedding vectors generated: 1,200,000 vectors/month
- Primary model family (chat/generation): open-llama-13b-16k (float16)
- Reranker model: distilled-bert-rerank-v1
- Average generation seq length (prompt+response): 280 tokens
- Percent of requests with long context (>4k): 6%
- Current unit costs (Mariner invoiced): generation $0.0135 per 1k tokens, embeddings $0.022 per vector, rerank $0.003 per request

Baseline monthly cost table (rounded):
- Generation: 3,600,000k tokens / 1k * $0.0135 = $48,600  (note: this includes both prompt & completion)
- Embeddings: 1,200,000 * $0.022 = $26,400
- Reranker: 450,000 requests * $0.003 = $1,350
- Cross-route discounts / committed credits applied: -$29,550 (Mariner has existing reserved capacity credits applied across generation/embeddings)
- Net baseline spend (invoice): $46,800/month (this matches Mariner CFO provided MRR)

Observed performance & ops constraints:
- Peak qps: 75 sustained, spikes to 180 for 3–6 minutes daily (batch windows exist)
- SLO: 99th percentile tail latency < 450ms for interactive flows (clinical-assistant)
- Security: PII redaction required pre-embedding, cannot push plaintext to third-party cache without customer KMS acceptance

Redwood Optimize recommendations applied in scenario analysis (short descriptions):
1) Model routing: route non-clinical/templated prompts to a cheaper 6B variant (quantized) with similarity check; only clinical-critical prompts hit 13B.
2) Mixed precision & quantization: int8 quantization profile for 13B in Dedicated pool, int4 for 6B experimental routes where acceptable.
3) Prefix/KV caching: cache common long-context prefixes for the clinical-assistant (approx 12% of requests share >60% identical prefix content).
4) Embedding batching + dedupe: batch embeddings up to 64 vectors per request server-side and dedupe near-duplicates before generation.
5) Batching policy changes: enable continuous batching with 12ms max latency floor for non-interactive batched routes (ingestion jobs).
6) Rerank dedup: route top-3 candidates to a small reranker + fallback only when score range ambiguous (reduce full rerank calls by ~33%).

Scenario modeling (conservative / likely / aggressive):
Assumptions shared across scenarios: token volume unchanged; embedding vector counts unchanged; reserved credits still applied but redistributed per routing.

Conservative scenario (safe rollout):
- 6B takeover: 28% of generation requests moved to 6B quantized (templated/help flows)
- 13B quantized with int8: applied to 72% remaining generation traffic
- Embedding batching saves 18% cost (smaller batching due to latency constraints)
- Prefix cache hit rate: 9% effective savings on generation tokens
Estimated monthly costs:
- Generation: $32,000
- Embeddings: $21,700
- Reranker: $1,100
- Net after credits: $30,000
- Savings vs baseline: $16,800 (36%)

Likely scenario (expected at maturity of rollout):
- 6B takeover: 40% of generation requests
- 13B int8: remaining 60%
- Embedding batching saves 28%
- Prefix cache hit rate: 12%
Estimated monthly costs:
- Generation: $26,400
- Embeddings: $19,008
- Reranker: $900
- Net after credits: $24,400
- Savings vs baseline: $22,400 (48%)

Aggressive scenario (full quantization + aggressive batching):
- 6B takeover: 50%
- 13B int8+perf kernels and additional sequence trimming: remaining 50%
- Embedding batching saves 40%
- Prefix cache hit rate: 18%
Estimated monthly costs:
- Generation: $23,100
- Embeddings: $15,840
- Reranker: $800
- Net after credits: $22,400
- Savings vs baseline: $24,400 (52%)

Risks and mitigation:
- Quality regression: Quantization can introduce hallucinations in clinical-critical prompts. Mitigation: canary traffic split (1% traffic to quantized 13B for 2 weeks), add automatic rollback on eval regression score drop > 0.6% on our clinical eval set (ticket JIRA-OPT-3453).
- Latency SLO slip: Batching & caching may add tail latency for interactive flows. Mitigation: keep clinical-assistant routed to Dedicated low-latency pool when P95 rises past 300ms; fall back to fp16 13B if needed.
- Data security: caching prefix content requires KMS-approved encryption at rest; coordinate with Mariner security (Confluence thread) and update contract addendum.

Operational rollout plan (30/60/90 day cadence):
- 0–14 days: implement instrumentation hooks, snapshot 30k queries for offline QA, create traffic labels (templated vs clinical-critical), baseline metrics. (Owners: Solutions Eng Jonah Reed, TE: Priya Singh)
- 15–45 days: start 6B routing on templated flows (canary 5% -> 25% -> 50%), enable int8 profile in dedicated pool for non-critical traffic; enable embedding batching for jobs. Monitor quality metrics.
- 46–75 days: expand prefix caching to 12% effective hit rate, tune batch sizes for embeddings; run customer-facing readout showing 30-day realized delta.
- 76–90 days: adopt full policy recommended if QA pass, update billing allocation and reserved credit mapping, convert to steady-state autoscaling rules.

Measurement & checkpoints (what we'll monitor):
- Cost by route (daily granular): generation / embeddings / rerank
- Quality safeguards: clinical eval score delta, hallucination counts, human-in-loop review volume
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 for clinical-assistant and ingestion pipelines
- Cache telemetry: hit rate, staleness, size of cached KV per prefix

Open questions / decisions required from Mariner:
- Acceptable QA regression threshold for clinical flows? (propose 0.5%)
- KMS coverage for prefix cache keys—can they sign off for us to host encrypted cache?
- Legal: update on reserved credit reallocation and attribution across route buckets.

Next steps (immediate action items):
- Share this sheet with Mariner cadence lead and request access to the 30k query snapshot (due 2025-11-18).
- Create JIRA epic combining OPT-3421, OPT-3453 for rollout tracking.
- Schedule 60-min readout on 2025-11-25 with SE + Mariner security.

Appendix A — quick sensitivity table (monthly generation only, simplified):
- Baseline gen cost: $48,600
- If 25% of tokens moved to 6B @ 40% unit cost = new gen $36,450 (25% * 0.4 + 75% * 1.0 baseline units)
- If prefix cache hits 12% and effectively reduces billed tokens by 12% across remaining traffic -> additional $4,300 savings

Notes (informal):
- This doc is a working draft. Numbers are rounded; final invoice reconciliation can differ after reserved credit re-attribution.
- Keep an eye on inbound product changes from Serving Runtime team (perf kernels scheduled v2.9.1) that could materially improve int8 perf; if released during canary we should re-run likely scenario.

-- Aisha (SE lead)
